subject: Hosted evaluation — quickstart access, endpoints, and rate-profile clarifications
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
Cc: FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — quick checklist + a couple of clarifying Qs

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the team appreciated the walkthrough of the inference flow and your explanations around routing/fallback. A few quick items we discussed that I want to capture so we can move toward a short hosted evaluation: 

- Quickstart access: can you confirm what sandbox endpoints we get and whether API keys are scoped per-project? We want to sandbox a single environment for devs + a separate one for analytics.
- Rate limits: what are the default throttle values for Hosted (requests/sec and token/sec)? Do those apply per-key or per-account?
- Data residency / retention: we have customers in EU; for the eval can we confirm that data processed via Hosted is not replicated outside us-west by default? Also what is the default token retention window for logs/trace?
- Decision path: our security team will push on hosted vs dedicated vs VPC. Any quick guidance on the criteria you recommend for FinLytics to pick Hosted for evaluation vs spinning up Dedicated?

Attaching our SOC2 evidence request (high level) for your security team to acknowledge.

Next steps: are you available for a 30-minute technical preflight tomorrow where we can lock scope and endpoints? If Hosted works for the eval we'll likely request a 2-week sandbox with a modest burst allowance.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Product
FinLytics

---
Attachment: FinLytics_SOC2_Request.pdf (attached by customer)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-05-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — quick checklist + a couple of clarifying Qs

Samir — great to meet you and the FinLytics crew this morning. Quick answers below and a proposed plan.

1) Sandbox endpoints & keys
- We’ll provision two sandbox projects ("finlytics-dev" and "finlytics-analytics") with separate API keys scoped to each project. Keys are per-project and you can rotate/delete them independently.

2) Default Hosted rate limits (initial evaluation tier)
- Default: 60 requests/minute and 150k tokens/minute per-project API key.
- Rate limits are enforced per-key by default; account-wide caps can be configured if you prefer a single envelope.
- We can temporarily increase the tokens/min for your eval window (see proposed burst below).

3) Data residency & retention
- Hosted evaluation endpoints in the US-west region will not replicate data to other regions by default.
- Standard diagnostic logs are retained for 30 days; you can request a shorter retention window (7 days) for the sandbox.
- All in-flight and at-rest data is encrypted (AES-256) and keys can be managed via our KMS integration for production — for hosted eval we manage keys but we can sign an NDA/SoW that notes the handling rules.

4) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — short guidance
- Hosted: fastest time-to-value, simplest onboarding; good for feature validation and lightweight customer data.
- Dedicated: recommended when you need predictable throughput and contractual isolation (monthly commit).
- Private (VPC/on-prem): required if you have strict residency, audit, or regulated storage rules.
- For an initial two-week evaluation we usually recommend Hosted in your preferred region, then move to Dedicated once you hit sustained throughput or compliance thresholds.

Proposed evaluation offer (what we can do quickly):
- Provision 2 sandbox projects (dev + analytics) today.
- Temporary burst: up to 100k tokens/day additional for two weeks (no additional cost for the first week, limited blowout insurance).
- Short preflight tech call: 30 minutes tomorrow at 10:00am PT to lock endpoints, retention, and sign off on the SOC2 doc.

Attached: Hosted_Quickstart_Playbook.pdf (sandbox onboarding), Rate_Table.csv (default + burst tiers).

If that looks good I’ll loop in CS (Monica) to create the sandbox and submit the trial-burst for approval.

Thanks — I’ll wait for your confirmation on the 10am PT slot.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Hosted_Quickstart_Playbook.pdf (stub), Rate_Table.csv (stub)

Vanessa — quick internal note before you lock the call:

- I approve the two-week trial with a temporary 100k tokens/day burst (attach approval stub). We should cap total burst to 2x baseline for safety.
- Finance will require a short SOW for the extended burst if they go beyond two weeks; we should get procurement prepped.
- Confirm region = us-west (customer is US headquartered) — if they later request EU we need a dedicated footprint conversation.

Monica — can you spin up the sandbox projects once Van confirms and add the trial-burst ticket? Put the sandbox retention at 7 days for this eval (per Vanessa's note) and log SOC2 request in the customer folder.

Ben

Vanessa — thanks, that all looks sensible and the proposed approach should work for our eval. Confirming:

- 10:00am PT tomorrow works for the tech preflight (we’ll send calendar invite).
- We accept the two sandbox projects and the 2-week trial with a 100k tokens/day temporary burst. Please set retention to 7 days for the sandbox.
- For procurement: please share a short SOW and the standard eval terms (NDA already signed). Ideally we’d have a DocuSign-ready SOW to route to our procurement team.
- Security ask: our security team will want a named contact on your side for the SOC2 questionnaire; could Monica be the point?

I’ve attached the SOC2 questionnaire again for your reference.

Samir

FinLytics
